classification.difficultyReason: Use the symmetric square-sum identity and explain why a negative result contradicts real roots; the dependent parts scaffold this familiar connection.

content.prompt:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of $3x^2+2x+4=0$.

(a) Find the value of $\alpha^2+\beta^2$.

(b) Hence explain why the roots of this quadratic are not real.

answer.short: (a) $-\dfrac{20}{9}$; (b) The sum of two real squares cannot be negative, but $\alpha^2+\beta^2=-\dfrac{20}{9}$.
answer.worked:
(a) $\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac23$, $\alpha\beta=\dfrac43$.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+\beta^2&=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta\\&=\left(-\frac23\right)^2-2\left(\frac43\right)\\&=\frac49-\frac{24}{9}\\&=-\frac{20}{9}\end{aligned}$$
(b) If both roots were real, $\alpha^2\geq0$ and $\beta^2\geq0$, so their sum would be non-negative. Since $\alpha^2+\beta^2=-\dfrac{20}{9}$, the roots are not real.
